item.title: Avoid eager task start in config flow steps
item.content: When a config flow step creates a background task whose result determines the next step, pass eager_start=False to hass.async_create_task so the progress step is always returned before the task runs; eager execution makes config flow tests flaky.

review_comments: Changes look good but `tests/components/homeassistant_hardware/test_config_flow.py:653 test_config_flow_firmware_download_fails_but_not_required` seems to be very flaky for me now.

Looks good. `eager_start=False` fixes the flaky config flow tests at the source, and I couldn't reproduce the flakiness at 4b3c4ca0ec6. Two small, non-blocking nits are inline.

<details><summary>Verification of the flaky-test fix</summary>

`_install_firmware_step` now always returns the progress step before the task has run, so whether `universal_silabs_flasher.firmware` is already imported no longer matters. A small pytest plugin that slows down that import and evicts the module before every test made `test_config_flow_firmware_download_fails_but_not_required` and `test_config_flow_doesnt_downgrade` fail at f5049d456f8. At this head all five affected suites (homeassistant_hardware, homeassistant_connect_zbt2, homeassistant_yellow, homeassistant_sky_connect, otbr; 368 tests) pass with it, and the two hardware config flow test files passed 15 of 15 repeated runs.

No user-visible change: on real hardware the flashing context and the probe do real I/O, so the eagerly started task was already suspended before it finished and the progress step was always shown. Moving `installing_firmware_name` is safe because `_install_firmware` is only ever started from `_install_firmware_step`, an

Nit, not blocking: this module-level import puts pygbl and pyelftools (`pygbl.elf` imports `elftools` at load time) on the import path of every ZHA and OTBR setup, since both import `homeassistant_hardware.util` from their `__init__`. On dev, importing `homeassistant.components.otbr` or `homeassistant.components.zha` loads none of the firmware stack until the hardware is actually probed or flashed; #183283 moved these imports behind `async_import_module` for that reason. With this PR both now load `pygbl` and `elftools` (about 60 ms of cumulative import time when importing otbr here, about 120 ms for `import pygbl` in a fresh interpreter). It could stay lazy like the other flasher modules:

```python
PYGBL_MODULE = "pygbl"
...
pygbl_module = await async_import_module(hass, PYGBL_MODULE)
fw_image = await hass.async_add_executor_job(
    pygbl_module.parse_firmware_image, fw_data
)
```

with the tests patching `pygbl.parse_firmware_image`, the way they patched the USF path before. By the time this runs the flasher module, which imports pygbl, is already loaded, so the import takes the `sys.modules` fast path and doesn't add a new executor hop.

Small follow-up from the split: 1.2.0 moved the Spinel protocol out into `aiospinel` (`flasher.py` now does `from aiospinel import SpinelProtocol`). In 1.1.0 it lived in `universal_silabs_flasher/spinel.py` and logged under the `universal_silabs_flasher` logger. That logger is listed in the `loggers` of zha, homeassistant_connect_zbt2, homeassistant_sky_connect and homeassistant_yellow, but `aiospinel` logs under its own name and isn't listed anywhere. Enabling debug logging on those integrations no longer shows the Spinel probe traffic. Adding `"aiospinel"` next to `"universal_silabs_flasher"` in those four manifests would keep it. pygbl has no logger of its own, so it doesn't need an entry.
Looks good! Flashed a ZBT-2 with Thread + Zigbee firmware without issues as well.
